name: NextEra Energy, Inc.

profile.description: NextEra Energy generates, stores, transmits, distributes, and sells electric power to retail and wholesale customers in North America. Operates through Florida Power & Light (FPL), the largest electric utility in Florida serving approximately 6 million customer accounts, and NextEra Energy Resources (NEER), the world's largest generator of wind and solar energy with approximately 36 GW of net generating capacity. Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.15 beat consensus by $0.07, with management targeting the high end of $3.92-$4.02 FY2026 guidance and record renewables backlog of 35.1 GW [1][2].

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): NextEra transformed from a traditional Florida utility (FPL Group) into the world's largest generator of wind and solar energy and then announced the $67B acquisition of Dominion Energy in May 2026, creating the world's largest utility and positioning NEE as the go-to energy partner for AI data centers with plans for 30+ data center hubs across the U.S. [1][2]. Q2 2026 added a record 3.6 GW to the renewables backlog, bringing total to 35.1 GW. This represents serial transformative reinvention from a regional utility to a global clean energy technology leader. AI Deployment (1/2): NEE has partnered with Google Cloud in a strategic energy and technology partnership to accelerate AI growth, applying AI to grid management, generation forecasting, and renewable asset optimization [2]. CEO Ketchum joined the AI Infrastructure Partnership and the company runs annual Hack Weeks for innovation, but specific AI-driven revenue or cost savings have not been separately quantified. Market Share (2/2): World's largest generator of wind and solar energy, operator of the largest electric utility in Florida (FPL, ~6M accounts), and the pending Dominion acquisition would make NEE the largest regulated utility globally by any standard measure [1][2]. Product Pipeline (2/2): Record 35.1 GW renewables backlog with specific projects and customer commitments including multi-gigawatt data center hub deals; 15 GW data center hub development target by 2035; Dominion Energy merger targeting H2 2027 close creates clear capacity expansion timeline [1][2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): Utilities invest primarily through capital expenditures rather than traditional R&D; NEE's innovation occurs through project development and deployment rather than laboratory research.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): CEO Ketchum positions NextEra as 'a technology company that delivers electricity,' with a purpose centered on powering a cleaner, more sustainable energy future through renewable energy leadership [2]. This goes beyond typical utility rhetoric and connects the company's work to decarbonization and the energy transition. Strategic decisions — investing billions in wind, solar, and storage when fossil fuels were more profitable — trace back to this vision. Distinctive and specific among utility peers. Community Impact (1/2): FPL operates community storm hardening programs that protect Florida customers, and NextEra supports general corporate philanthropy and sustainability initiatives including participation in the UN Global Compact and Sustainable Stock Exchanges Initiative [3]. However, the ghost candidate election scandal involving FPL and environmental justice concerns around the Sabal Trail Pipeline (42% owned, with 84% of route near communities of color) temper the community impact assessment [3]. Employee Retention (1/2): CEO Ketchum succeeded long-tenured Jim Robo in 2022, providing leadership continuity; 17,400 employees across regulated and competitive business segments. No specific voluntary turnover data or exceptional retention metrics publicly available. Insider Buying (0/2): Recent insider data shows significant net selling — multiple officers sold vested equity awards in 2026. No meaningful net insider buying identified.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Dividend stock with strong results across most dimensions. Forward P/E of 17.9 comfortably beats the 20 target (score 1.0) following the stock's pullback from its Dominion-acquisition highs [1]. Profit margin of 32.4% is exceptional for a regulated utility (score 1.0). D/E of 161.7% is the primary drag — capital-intensive utility infrastructure and renewables development drive high leverage, though typical for the sector (score 0.60) [1]. ROE of 11.7% falls short of the 15% target but is solid for a regulated utility (score 0.78). Revenue growth YoY of 12.4% exceeds the 10% target (score 1.0), while 5-year revenue CAGR of approximately 9% approaches target (score 0.93). Dividend metrics are exceptional: 53+ consecutive years of payments (score 1.0, 2x weight), 30 consecutive years of growth (score 1.0), sustainable 53.5% payout ratio (score 0.78), and 10.1% 5-year dividend growth CAGR exceeding the 6% target (score 1.0, 2x weight). Liquidity floor cleared: 11.6M avg volume × $78.28 = $907M daily.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (9/9): Electric utilities are categorically immune to AI disruption — generating, transmitting, and distributing electricity requires physical power plants, transmission lines, substations, and distribution networks that AI cannot replace [1]. Moreover, AI infrastructure growth is a direct and massive demand driver for NEE: data centers consume enormous amounts of electricity, and NextEra has signed multi-gigawatt renewable energy contracts with technology companies specifically to power AI workloads, with 6 GW of AI-related projects in backlog and 15 GW data center hub target by 2035 [2]. FPL's regulated monopoly serving 6 million Florida customers has zero AI substitution risk, and NEER's wind and solar generation serves a growing market as AI electrification accelerates energy demand. CEO Ketchum sees AI-driven data center power demand as 'only renewables can fuel' at the scale required [2]. AI Opportunity (1/1): NEE generates quantifiable revenue from powering AI infrastructure through multi-gigawatt renewable energy contracts with technology companies, and the Google Cloud strategic partnership commits both companies to 'accelerate AI growth and transform the energy industry' [2]. The $67B Dominion acquisition positions the combined entity to build 30+ data center hubs across the U.S., directly monetizing AI-driven electricity demand.

infinite_game.summary: NextEra Energy demonstrates strong infinite game characteristics in its strategic vision and courage to invest in clean energy transformation, but organizational culture weaknesses and the relatively new leadership tenure temper the overall assessment. CEO Ketchum's vision of NextEra as 'a technology company that delivers electricity' and the company's multi-decade pivot from traditional utility to world's largest renewables generator reflect deeply infinite thinking. The $67B Dominion acquisition and record 35.1 GW backlog demonstrate long-horizon strategic courage [1][2].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Powering a cleaner, more sustainable energy future through renewable energy leadership is a genuine purpose that connects NextEra's work to one of humanity's most important challenges [2]. CEO Ketchum's framing of NEE as 'a technology company that delivers electricity' elevates the purpose beyond traditional utility operations. Strategic decisions — investing tens of billions in wind, solar, and storage when fossil fuels were more immediately profitable — trace back to this vision. However, the framing is relatively new under Ketchum (CEO since 2022), and the company's involvement in the ghost candidate scandal and environmental justice concerns around the Sabal Trail Pipeline create tension with the stated purpose [3].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): CEO Ketchum assumed the role in 2022 following Jim Robo's long tenure, providing leadership continuity, and the 17,400-person workforce operates across regulated and competitive segments. However, multiple officers sold shares worth millions in 2026 equity award vestings, suggesting routine financial hedging rather than conviction buying. No specific voluntary turnover data, employee satisfaction scores, or evidence of exceptional psychological safety distinguish NextEra from utility industry norms. The ghost candidate political scandal involving FPL suggests governance weaknesses that may extend to organizational culture [3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): CEO Ketchum has emphasized that it is critically important to 'pivot and move to where the opportunities are while managing the disruption that can challenge this industry' [2]. NextEra maintains a team dedicated to embracing disruptive forces reshaping the energy industry and seeking new ways to disrupt its own company. This competitive framing focuses on self-improvement and adaptation rather than defeating specific rivals, reflecting genuine infinite game thinking about competition.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): NextEra fundamentally transformed from a traditional Florida electric utility (FPL Group) into the world's largest generator of wind and solar energy — a multi-decade pivot that redefined both the company and industry expectations for utility innovation [1][2]. Building a 35.1 GW contracted renewables backlog while operating a regulated utility is a transformative reinvention driven by the clean energy vision. The $67B Dominion acquisition represents the next existential pivot — from clean energy leader to the world's largest utility with AI data center infrastructure capabilities.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (2/2): NextEra invested aggressively in wind and solar energy when fossil fuels were more immediately profitable, spending tens of billions building the world's largest renewables portfolio over two decades [2]. The $67B Dominion Energy acquisition announced in May 2026 is a bold, transformative bet justified by Ketchum's conviction that 'scale matters more than ever' as AI-driven electricity demand surges [1]. Management targets 8%+ adjusted EPS CAGR through 2032, demonstrating a long-horizon investment framework. The consistent pattern — renewables pivot, Google partnership, data center hubs, Dominion acquisition — reflects leadership that consistently chooses long-term capability over short-term optimization.

investment_thesis: NextEra Energy at $78.28 with a $163.3B market cap is executing a transformative strategy to become the world's largest and most diversified utility through the pending $67B Dominion Energy acquisition, which positions NEE as the go-to energy partner for AI data centers with plans for 30+ hubs across the U.S. [1][2]. Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.15 beat consensus by $0.07, with management targeting the high end of $3.92-$4.02 FY2026 guidance and 8%+ EPS CAGR through 2032 [1]. Record renewables origination of 3.6 GW in Q2 alone brought total backlog to 35.1 GW, while the Google Cloud strategic partnership underscores NEE's position as the energy backbone of AI growth [2]. The 30-year dividend growth streak (10.1% 5-year CAGR) with a sustainable 53.5% payout ratio and 3.18% yield at a forward P/E of just 17.9 make this a compelling dividend growth holding at a reasonable valuation.
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on integration risk, leverage, and governance concerns. The $67B Dominion acquisition faces regulatory hurdles across multiple state commissions, FERC, and the NRC, with Virginia political leaders expressing wariness and environmental groups filing motions arguing the merger application was incomplete [3]. D/E of 161.7% will increase significantly post-merger, making the combined entity highly sensitive to interest rate movements at a time when rates remain elevated. The ghost candidate election scandal involving FPL — with five people criminally charged — and a securities class action alleging executives misled investors represent material governance risks [3]. Environmental justice concerns around the Sabal Trail Pipeline (84% of route near communities of color) and lobbying controversy ($20M spent to block a clean energy transmission line in Maine) create reputational headwinds that contrast with the clean energy mission. Free cash flow is deeply negative at -$17.8B due to massive capital expenditure requirements for renewables development, making NEE dependent on capital markets access for continued growth.
key_catalysts: Pending $67B Dominion Energy acquisition creating the world's largest utility with plans for 30+ data center hubs, positioned as the premier energy partner for AI infrastructure at unprecedented scale with H2 2027 target close [1][2]

Record 35.1 GW renewables backlog with 3.6 GW added in Q2 2026 alone, plus the Google Cloud strategic partnership to 'accelerate AI growth and transform the energy industry' driving structural demand for clean power [2]

Attractive valuation at 17.9x forward earnings with a 3.18% dividend yield, 30-year growth streak (10.1% 5yr CAGR), and management guiding 8%+ adjusted EPS CAGR through 2032 supported by regulated rate base growth and AI-driven electricity demand [1]
key_risks: Dominion acquisition regulatory risk across multiple state commissions, FERC, and NRC with Virginia political opposition and environmental group challenges that could delay, modify, or block the $67B deal [3]
Deeply negative free cash flow of -$17.8B and post-merger leverage escalation on existing D/E of 161.7%, creating interest rate sensitivity and capital markets dependence at a time of elevated rates

Governance concerns from the FPL ghost candidate scandal (five criminal charges, securities class action) and environmental justice controversies that create reputational risk and potential regulatory scrutiny [3]
